Both `cargo test -q -p ucal --no-fail-fast` and `cargo test -q -p xtask --no-fail-fast` pass. Changes are left uncommitted as requested, confined to `crates/ucal/src/clock.rs`.

## Summary

Implemented smoothing for `Session::reading` in `crates/ucal/src/clock.rs`: a single reading can no longer land an arbitrarily large forward wall-clock correction in one call. Each call is now capped at `last + max(elapsed_since_previous_call, CATCH_UP_FLOOR_NANOS)` (a 1-second floor, chosen against `ucal wallclock`'s 50ms redraw cadence), so:

- Ordinary ticking is unaffected (elapsed time already exceeds the floor).
- Backward steps behave exactly as before (unaffected by the new cap).
- Large forward corrections (e.g. NTP step, VM resume) are walked toward at ≥1 second of progress per call instead of appearing as an instant leap on `ucal wallclock`'s face — while still being fully adopted, never refused.

Updated the module/struct docs to state the new rule, replaced the old `a_forward_step_is_accepted` test (which asserted an instant full jump) with `a_forward_step_is_capped_in_a_single_call`, and added `a_capped_forward_step_is_still_reached` to verify the correction is eventually fully adopted over calls at the TUI's real cadence, monotonically.
